'''''Lophocereus''''' is a [[genus]] of [[Cactus|cacti]]. It has often been merged into the genus ''[[Pachycereus]]'', but was separated in a 2019 revision of ''Pachycereus'',<ref name=AriaTerr09/> and is accepted by Plants of the World Online {{As of|2021|March|lc=yes}}. 
==Description==
''Lophocereus'' are bushy cacti, little or very branched from the base, with 4-15 pronounced ribs. They have variable spines depending on the species. In summer, on the sides of the stem, on the pseudocephalium in ''L. schotti'', self-sterile tubular flowers of reddish, orange, or greenish color, sometimes yellow, emerge. It has scales on the outside. The flowers are pollinated by insects and bats. Its fruits are red globose and its seeds are black and shiny.<ref name="Anon. u329">{{cite web | title=Volumen 4: Los Cactus. Universidad de Valencia E.G. p. 103 | url=http://jardibotanic.org/fotos/pdf/publicacion_2_111_CACTUS-ESP-BAJAaaa.pdf | access-date=2023-11-02}}</ref>

==Uses==
Its cultivation is very widespread in family gardens, to prevent erosion and for its fruits, and in gardens for its ornamental value.

The fruits are consumed fresh or dried and used to make sauces, ice cream and jams.

The stems serve as fodder. They are used as medicine for earaches, diarrhea, kidney and bladder problems, ulcers, tumors, even cirrhosis. It is also used to dye hair and prevent hair loss.

Its wood is used in construction and planted close together they serve as fences for corrals.<ref name="Anon. u329"/>
